summary: A line of your own: Neither big party will nominate you, and {organizer} asks how you get on the ballot.
realLife: One life: A Socialist Alternative candidate, she sued the state to list her party on the 2012 ballot, lost that race, and in 2013 beat a long-serving Seattle council member on a $15 minimum wage platform. Another: He ran for New York mayor in 1933 on a Fusion ticket backed by reformers, Republicans and anti-Tammany Democrats, and won. Another: He left the Republicans and won the 1990 Connecticut governor's race on his own A Connecticut Party line with about 40 percent in a three-way race.
gates: Candidate not nominated by a major party.
weights: How unpopular the major parties are on record.
How many candidates split the vote.
choices: run on a small party's line, suing if it is kept off
run on a fusion line with reformers of both parties
